reason: Appendages tied to the calyx are real (Campanulaceae appendages in the sinuses, Boraginaceae), but the examples ('with c. 6 ± thickened terete curv...') do not show which structure is meant: sinus appendages, lobe outgrowths or emergences. In palm floras 'leaf-segments ... on each side' are leaflets (leaflet PO_0020049), but in palmate palms and in dissected leaves (Apiaceae, Ranunculaceae) the segments are lobes (leaf lamina lobe PO_0025517). reason: A real structure that floras describe and count; PO has flower fascicle (PO_0025323, synonym 'bundle') only for groups of flowers, and staminal tube (FLOPO_0986013) for a single fused tube. It is found across several families, so it should be proposed to PO upstream.

A piece of a sentence ('Disseminule comprising a floret'). It states what the dispersal unit is made of; the part is floret, which already maps to flower (rule C261).

Narrower: a cyme whose branches all arise from about one point, so it looks like an umbel. 'Umbellate' is the shape; the bearer is the cyme inflorescence. Not umbel inflorescence (PO_0030129), which is racemose.
Narrower: aciculi (FNA Rubus, Rosa) are slender, needle-like prickles, often gland-tipped, so 'stipitate-glandular or eglandular' and length fit a prickle. Not trichome: they are emergences.

A rule would need plant cell (PO_0009002) as part of the lamellae of a non-vascular leaf (PO_0025075), but PO has no lamella class to name the whole. Mapping to 'cell of the non-vascular leaf' would put the lamella-cell shape ('marginal cells in section pyriform') on every leaf cell. It needs a lamella class or a curator decision.
